gap.prompt: I ___ in this town since I was a child.
If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel the trip.
gap.explain: Use the present simple after if.

gap.prompt: She said she ___ finish the project by Friday.
gap.explain: Use would for reported future plans.

gap.prompt: This is ___ interesting book I have ever read.
gap.explain: Use the most with longer adjectives.

gap.prompt: You ___ see a doctor if the pain continues.
The emails ___ by the assistant every morning.
gap.explain: Use the present passive for a regular action.

gap.prompt: I’m looking forward to ___ you next week.

gap.explain: Use the past tense in reported questions.

mistake.sentence: She has visited Paris last year.
mistake.explain: Use the past simple with last year.

mistake.sentence: I am living here since January.
He suggested to meet at the station.
If I will have time, I will call you.
mistake.explain: Use the present simple after if.

mistake.sentence: This hotel is more cheaper than that one.
She told that she was busy.
mistake.explain: Use said that, or told me.

phrase.prompt: We need to ___ up with a better plan.
phrase.explain: Come up with means think of.

phrase.prompt: I can’t ___ up with this noise any longer.
phrase.explain: Put up with means accept something unpleasant.

phrase.prompt: She decided to ___ up smoking last month.
phrase.explain: Give up means stop doing something.

phrase.prompt: The meeting was ___ off because of the snow.
He wants to ___ for a job at the new company.
I need to ___ an eye on my suitcase.
phrase.explain: Keep an eye on means watch carefully.

formation.prompt: She showed great ___ during the difficult week. (STRONG)
formation.explain: Use the noun form of strong.

formation.prompt: It is ___ to check the weather before a trip. (USE)
He made a quick ___ to change the plan. (DECIDE)
formation.explain: Use the noun form of decide.
Use an adverb to describe how it works.

dictation.sentence: I have lived in this town since I was a child.
alternatives: I've lived in this town since I was a child.

dictation.sentence: She said she would finish the project by Friday.
The meeting was called off because of the snow.
We should leave early to avoid traffic.
He is looking for a job in logistics.
This is the most interesting book I have ever read.
alternatives: This is the most interesting book I've ever read.
